issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies `Stock.add(String): void`, but both the template and the reference solution implement `Stock.add(String)` with return type `int` (returning the updated quantity or -1). This signature mismatch makes it unclear what students should implement and can lead to failing compilation/tests if they follow the UML literally.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification with the provided code by changing the UML to `add(String): int` and briefly documenting the meaning of the return value (new quantity, -1 if ingredient not found). Alternatively, if `void` is intended, change template/solution to `void add(String)` and update all call sites accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement first describes the `SealSaloon` stock attribute as a non-static `final Stock stock` (per-instance), but later explicitly requires `stock` to be `static` (shared across instances). The reference solution follows the latter (`private static final Stock stock`). This contradiction can mislead students about whether stock is shared or per saloon instance and affects how methods like `acceptSupplyDelivery`/`calculateTotalPrice` should be implemented.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (a) update the earlier description/UML to clearly state `static final Stock stock` (shared across all `SealSaloon` instances), or (b) remove the static requirement and adapt the solution/tests to use an instance-level `final Stock stock`.
